finding_resolutions.pass2_finding: WP-006 (blocking) — the currency gate's predicate `s.state <> 'active'` falsely refuses a run-off supersession the engine would still select.
finding_resolutions.evidence: WP-006 required_changes now names `s.selectable = false` as THE predicate, with the enumerated equivalent offered and a 'pick one, comment which and why' instruction; the mandatory negative test test_a_run_off_supersession_does_not_refuse_execution is present with a run_off fixture and an explicit SUCCEEDS expectation; the acceptance criterion is restated as 'refuses ... and ONLY such a run', naming retire_now and retired as refused and run-off as not refused. Verified at source: backend/db/migrations/0002_clause_registry.sql:247-252 derives `state` (superseded whenever any supersession row exists) and :253-258 derives `selectable` as `(not v.retired and (v.expires_on is null or v.expires_on >= current_date) and (s.id is null or s.predecessor_disposition = 'run_off' or s.effective_on > current_date))`, under the schema's own comment 'What resolution actually asks. A run-off predecessor is superseded but still usable until it expires on its own.' cw.selectable_clause (0002:267-268) is `select * from cw.clause_version_state where selectable`, so `selectable` is the engine's own pool. The correction is right and is now guarded in both directions.

THE AUTHOR'S DISPUTE IS UPHELD AT SOURCE. Pass-2 asserted that 'grep confirms NOTHING after 0005_run_store.sql:288-298 grants cw_administrator SELECT on cw.run_summary, cw.run_contract, or cw.run_finding' and concluded all three run reads refuse an administrator. The cw.run_finding half of that premise is false: 0013_administrator.sql:290-306 explicitly grants SELECT on cw.run, cw.run_decision AND cw.run_finding to cw_administrator (line 296 of the grant list), and 0013:321-322 creates `administrator_reads on cw.run for select using (cw.app_role() = 'administrator')`. cw.run_finding's read_scoped policy is `exists (select 1 from cw.run r where r.run_id = run_finding.run_id)` (0005:283-284), carries no `to <role>` restriction, and its subquery is evaluated under row-level security — which for an administrator returns every run. GET /runs/findings therefore ANSWERS an administrator, with every run's findings. The views are the only gap: grep across 0001-0024 finds cw.run_summary and cw.run_contract granted only at 0005:293-296 (cw_auditor) and 0005:297 (cw_requester, cw_legal_reviewer, cw_legal_admin), so GET /runs and GET /runs/decisions refuse. rev3's non-uniform three-outcome table is correct as written and pass-2's uniform-refusal claim was wrong.

new_findings.issue: THE RECORDED 'ADMINISTRATOR GAP' IS FALSE, AND THE SIX-ROLE CORRECTION ADDED THIS PASS IS WHAT DISPROVES IT. WP-002's implementation note reads: 'cw_administrator holds INSERT on cw.audit_event (0013:257, policy at :275) but no INSERT on cw.run (0005:288-291). An administrator therefore passes the audit gate and receives an answer from this endpoint, and is refused only once WP-003 makes the endpoint persist ... test_runs.py asserts the current behaviour explicitly so WP-003 has to change the test on purpose.' But the same package's own loader sweep, added in this revision, establishes the opposite: 'cw_administrator is absent from every one of those grant lines and is refused the loader queries outright.' I verified all three at source — CLAUSE_SQL reads cw.clause_version_state (granted to five roles at 0002:352-354, not the administrator); LADDER_SQL reads cw.ladder_health (granted to five roles at 0003:669-670, not the administrator — 0013:292 grants only the base tables cw.ladder and cw.ladder_rung); RULE_SQL reads cw.active_conflict_rule (granted to five roles at 0004:237-238, not the administrator). WP-002's own ordering runs the three loader queries at step 6, BEFORE the answer at step 8, so an administrator is refused inside WP-002 with a 403 'not_permitted' from refusals.classify (refusals.py:88-89, INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGE). The specified test asserting the administrator receives an answer would fail, and WP-003's acceptance item 'an administrator is now refused, closing WP-002's recorded gap' closes a gap that never opens.
new_findings.correction: Replace WP-002's administrator note with the verified fact: from this package onwards an administrator calling POST /runs is refused BY THE DATABASE at the clause-library read, in its own words, because cw_administrator holds no SELECT on cw.clause_version_state, cw.ladder_health or cw.active_conflict_rule — the same absence the loader sweep asserts, and the same owner question 0018:170-190 records. Also drop the corresponding line from WP-002's risks ('The endpoint answers an administrator until WP-003 lands').
